title: Ibn al-Nafis & Michael Servetus (1213–1288 / 1511–1553) — Demolishing Galen's Invisible Septal Pores: Cairo's 1242 Anatomy Commentary, Paris Dissections Alongside Vesalius, Christianismi Restitutio's Hidden Pulmonary-Transit Pages, and the Green-Oak Pyre in Geneva

teenKit.tldr: For 1,300 years, medical science blindly trusted an ancient mistake that blood passed through invisible holes in the heart's center wall. Two rebels—Ibn al-Nafis in 13th-century Cairo and Michael Servetus in 16th-century Europe—risked everything to prove blood actually travels through the lungs to get oxygen.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how your blood picks up oxygen through the pulmonary transit is the foundation of modern medicine, reminding us that questioning established dogma is vital because blindly accepting authority can cost lives.
keyTakeaways: Claudius Galen's anatomical map of the human body went completely unquestioned for over 1,300 years because religious and cultural taboos banned human dissection.
In 1242, Syrian physician Ibn al-Nafis correctly deduced the pulmonary circulation of blood in Cairo, long before European scientists caught on.
Michael Servetus published the pulmonary transit discovery in his 1553 theological book, leading to his execution by burning at the stake for heresy.

vocab.meaning: Imaginary microscopic holes in the heart wall that Galen claimed allowed blood to pass from the right side to the left.
The real path blood takes, traveling from the heart through the lungs to pick up oxygen before returning to the body.
A principle or set of principles laid down by an authority as incontrovertibly true, often blocking scientific progress.
The protein in your red blood cells that changes shape at an atomic level to grab oxygen and turn your blood bright crimson.

quiz.question: Why did ancient medical authorities believe blood crossed directly through the middle wall of the heart?
options: Because Galen wrote it down and his authority went unquestioned for centuries
Because human dissections clearly proved invisible pores existed
Because Ibn al-Nafis published it in Cairo
Because X-ray crystallography confirmed it in Roman times
quiz.explanation: Galen's extensive writings became absolute dogma because human dissection was forbidden, preventing anyone from checking if his claims were real.

quiz.question: What major contribution did Ibn al-Nafis make in 1242?
options: He invented the microscope for looking at blood cells
He correctly explained that blood travels through the lungs rather than through invisible heart wall pores
He assisted Andreas Vesalius with human dissections in Paris
quiz.explanation: Ibn al-Nafis wrote a medical commentary in Cairo that demolished Galen's theory by accurately describing pulmonary transit.

quiz.question: What happened to Michael Servetus after he published his discovery hidden inside a theological book?
options: He was awarded the highest medical prize in Paris
He became the lead physician to the Pope
He was executed on a green-oak pyre in Geneva for heresy
He collaborated directly with William Harvey on De Motu Cordis
quiz.explanation: Servetus mixed radical medical observations with theology, leading to his tragic execution by burning in Geneva.
